summary: This sermon explores the 'way of the heart' as one spiritual pathway to encounter God, using King David's return of the Ark of the Covenant to Jerusalem as a biblical model. The preacher emphasizes that God meets us at the mercy seat—not in our theological boxes—and that His presence naturally inspires exuberant worship through celebration, music, and dancing, while still requiring reverence and holiness.
key_points: God dwells above the mercy seat, not in the box; we meet Him through mercy, not rigid theology
God's presence inspires joyful celebration—David danced, sang, and worshiped with all his might
Reverence matters: Uzzah's irreverent act shows grace is free but never cheap
Different spiritual 'stations' help us encounter God; the heart pathway engages through emotion and worship
Authentic worship flows from gratitude for God's faithfulness and transforms how we share our faith
big_idea: Encountering God's presence at the mercy seat—where grace and holiness meet—naturally produces exuberant, heartfelt worship that celebrates His faithfulness with our whole being.
title: Spiritual Stations: Heart
